```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(mizerMR)
```

# Stored capabilities

This development preview requires mizer 3.4.0.9012 or later. mizerMR records
its extension version and uses the `mizerMR` S3 class to participate in the
model's method chain. The multiple resources form one component named `MR`.
Its state is a resource-by-size number-density array on the full size grid;
its parameters contain resource-specific replenishment rates, capacities,
species interactions and the resource parameter table.

`setMultipleResources()` stores an assembled definition using
`mizer::setComponent()`. The definition supplies separate callbacks for custom
stepping, exact equations, convergence, biomass, tuning and transformations.
The state and parameter values remain separate from these declarations.
`mizer::getComponent(params, "MR")$definition` shows the stored specification.
Changing ordinary resource parameter values retains an author's current
capability choices.

The package implements the semi-chemostat, logistic and constant resource laws.
For those laws, `mrEquation()` returns the instantaneous derivative, while
`mizerMR_dynamics()` performs the established custom time step. The equation
and stepping contracts are separate: supplying a step does not imply that an
extension has supplied an equation or a convergence assessment.

# Rates and convergence

`projectEncounter.mizerMR()` adds resource encounter to the result of
`NextMethod()`. `projectResourceMort.mizerMR()` computes resource-specific
mortality using the same effective predator rates. The MR equation receives
these complete model rates, so resources remain coupled through the consumers.

`mrConvergence()` reports one quantitative measure and tolerance per resource.
The default measures the integrated absolute state derivative; an explicit
biomass criterion instead measures the absolute integrated derivative. Both
respect mizer's size-grid quadrature scheme. mizer combines these measures with
consumer and other component assessments.

The silenced core resource is explicitly declared a prescribed zero input.
Rows using `resource_constant` are likewise declared prescribed through a
structural mask. Zero observations, zero capacities and zero replenishment
rates never imply that a coordinate has been removed from the model.

Whole-model assessments include all dynamic resources. The current core
stability implementation does not assemble Jacobians for arbitrary dynamic
components, so whole-model stability of a dynamic MR model is unavailable.
An explicitly conditional analysis can hold the entire MR component fixed;
it describes that consumer subsystem and is labelled accordingly.

# Tuning strategies

The default MR strategy, `preserve_rate`, holds MR abundances during the
consumer steady-state search and adjusts resource capacities afterwards. The
alternative `preserve_capacity` adjusts replenishment rates. For example:

```r
params <- tuneSteadyState(
    params,
    strategies = c("component:MR" = "preserve_capacity")
)
```

These strategies declare their adjustable parameter paths, nonnegative bounds
and preserved values. Before a balancer runs, `mrTarget()` independently
constructs the effective source and loss targets at the candidate state.
`mrBalance()` implements the analytic, law-specific inverse. mizer verifies
that the returned model retains that state, the declared preserved values and
all effective equation quantities outside the authorised adjustment.
Infeasible constraints stop; no numerical fallback silently changes the
strategy.

A third strategy, `evolve`, advances MR states during the search and requires
the projection solver. It does not make an unsupported Newton treatment of
dynamic components appear supported.

MR explicitly adopts the known built-in reproduction specification through
`mizer::mizerReproductionDefinition()`. Adoption is restricted to recognised
effective rate and S3 method chains. A custom outer rate or reproduction method
requires an author declaration; merely retaining the same stored RDD name is
insufficient.

# Measurements

Use mizer's shared measurement interface to include resources:

```r
biomass <- mizer::getBiomass(params, include = c("species", "components"))
plot(biomass)
```

The MR callback returns one stable series per resource, including its label,
colour and linetype. It supports scalar weight and length bounds. Unsupported
filters are reported as unavailable rather than silently ignored. Consumer-only
measurement remains mizer's default, and `plotBiomass()` uses the same measured
object as `plot(getBiomass())`.

# Early transformations

MR declares support for adding, removing, reordering and renaming species,
changing the size grid, scaling abundance and scaling rates. The hooks run
before dependent construction or rate calculations, with the original model,
the candidate's new core layout and explicit species/grid maps.

Only the interaction matrix follows species rows. On a grid change, overlapping
MR state, replenishment rates and capacities retain their actual stored values,
including frozen values. New bins are constructed from the declared resource
power laws. There is no generic rule that resizes any array that happens to
have a matching dimension.

Abundance scaling changes MR abundance, capacity and the `kappa` resource
parameter together. Rate scaling changes MR replenishment rates and `r_pp`.
The core resource hook preserves its declared zero value. The hooks own only
these declared fields; mizer checks their ownership before accepting the result.

The thin `addSpecies.mizerMR()` method accepts the optional
`resource_interaction` matrix. It validates and aligns its species/resource
names, places a temporary request in MR-owned data, and calls `NextMethod()`.
The early hook consumes and removes that request. No late repair strips the
model's extension dispatch or recalculates interactions after rates have
already been built.

# Saved models and author-defined laws

`upgrade.mizerMR()` migrates old MR parameter layouts and registers capabilities
for legacy supported models. It leaves version stamping to mizer's upgrade
orchestrator and preserves current stored definitions. `validParams()` and
`readParams()` run that chain automatically.

Unknown resource laws may still supply their existing stepping function, and
MR biomass can still be measured. They do not acquire inferred equations,
autonomy, convergence, tuning or transformation support. Authors must provide
these contracts explicitly. In particular, defining `balance_<law>` no longer
registers balancing support. This prevents a model-changing operation from
proceeding with an extension that has not declared how its state and parameters
must be handled.
